combat_history.event: Philippine FA-50PHs conducted air strikes during the Marawi siege.
combat_history.significance: Combat employment in a Southeast Asian counter-insurgency.

modernization.description: AESA radar, beyond-visual-range missiles and aerial refuelling.
modernization.impact: Keeps the FA-50 credible as a light fighter, not just a trainer.

vulnerabilities.description: Limited range, payload and sensors versus true fighters.
vulnerabilities.context: A light/lead-in aircraft, not a frontline fighter.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Light air defence, ground attack and lead-in fighter training for budget-conscious air forces.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Often the high-end of a small air force, or a complement to F-16s.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Both chase Global-South light-fighter orders; the FA-50 is cheaper and trainer-derived, the Tejas a clean-sheet fighter.
The JF-17 is a heavier light fighter; the FA-50 leverages F-16 commonality and trainer roots.
The KF-21 is KAI's advanced fighter; the FA-50 is the affordable light end of the same pipeline.

doctrine.role: Affordable light combat aircraft and lead-in fighter trainer for budget-conscious air forces.
doctrine.employment: Light air defence and ground attack; the high-end of many small Southeast Asian air forces.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Cheap, supersonic, F-16-common capability available for export.
doctrine.threat_context: The connective light-combat aircraft of much of Southeast Asia and a pillar of Korean defence exports.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against the Tejas, JF-17 and (high-end) the KF-21.
